description: First 50 seeds only - testing 'starting well' quality

scoring_criteria.9: Perfect native speech in both languages
scoring_criteria.1-2: Marginal, no one would say this

worst_3_phrases.english: she wanted to ask you how long you have been
worst_3_phrases.spanish: ella quería preguntarte cuánto tiempo llevas
worst_3_phrases.reason: Incomplete sentence in both languages - 'how long you have been' what? Missing the activity (learning, working, etc.). The Spanish uses 'llevas' correctly for duration but the sentence trails off without completion.

worst_3_phrases.english: because she doesn't want to tonight
worst_3_phrases.spanish: porque ella no quiere esta noche
worst_3_phrases.reason: English is grammatically awkward - missing verb complement after 'want to'. Spanish similarly incomplete. Would need context like 'want to go out' or 'want to do it' to be natural.
English missing verb complement - 'want to' what? Spanish is similarly elliptical. Works only in very specific conversational context where the verb is implied.

summary.quality_assessment: Strong overall quality. Average of 7.82 indicates consistently good to excellent phrases. 70% scored 8 or 9 (excellent). Only 1 phrase below 6. Main issues are incomplete/elliptical sentences that lack context.

phrases.english: I wasn't thinking about how to feel better this morning
phrases.other: no estaba pensando en cómo sentirme mejor esta mañana
phrases.notes: Both natural, correct grammar. Imperfect tense used correctly. Reflexive 'sentirme' appropriate.

phrases.english: I wasn't thinking about how to answer
phrases.other: no estaba pensando en cómo responder
phrases.notes: Clean, natural construction in both languages.

phrases.english: or at the moment
phrases.other: o en este momento
phrases.notes: Fragment but both natural. Common connective phrase.

phrases.english: I don't want to read anything this morning
phrases.other: no quiero leer nada esta mañana
phrases.notes: Perfect in both languages. Natural word order, correct use of 'nada'.

phrases.english: about how to speak
phrases.other: en cómo hablar
phrases.notes: Fragment, correct. 'En' correctly used for 'about' with 'pensar'.

phrases.english: better than last night
phrases.other: mejor que anoche
phrases.notes: Perfect. 'Anoche' is the ideal single-word translation.

phrases.english: I'm looking forward to learning as soon as I can
phrases.other: tengo ganas de aprender tan pronto como pueda
phrases.notes: Excellent idiom choice. 'Tengo ganas de' captures the anticipation well. Subjunctive 'pueda' correct.

phrases.english: because it's a good thing to make mistakes
phrases.other: porque es algo bueno cometer errores
phrases.notes: Good. Could also be 'es bueno cometer errores' which is more direct, but this version is acceptable.

phrases.english: it's useful to speak better
phrases.other: es útil hablar mejor
phrases.notes: Clean, natural construction.

phrases.english: I would like to come back to speak Spanish tomorrow
phrases.other: me gustaría volver a hablar español mañana
phrases.notes: Good. 'Volver a' correctly means 'to do again'.

phrases.english: but I don't worry at the moment and I feel okay
phrases.other: pero no me preocupo en este momento y me siento bien
phrases.notes: Slightly clunky English compound, Spanish is fine. Reflexive verbs correct.

phrases.english: I'm a little tired at the moment
phrases.other: estoy un poco cansado en este momento
phrases.notes: Natural. Note: 'cansado' is masculine - would be 'cansada' for female speaker.

phrases.english: he doesn't want to interrupt the story
phrases.other: él no quiere interrumpir la historia
phrases.notes: Perfect. Natural in both languages.

phrases.english: or if I need to improve
phrases.other: o si necesito mejorar
phrases.notes: Clean fragment, natural in context.

phrases.english: I don't worry today
phrases.other: no me preocupo hoy
phrases.notes: Natural both languages. Reflexive correct.

phrases.english: because she doesn't want to tonight
phrases.other: porque ella no quiere esta noche
phrases.notes: English awkward - missing verb complement after 'want to'. Spanish similarly incomplete. Needs implied context.

phrases.english: you want to learn his name
phrases.other: quieres aprender su nombre
phrases.notes: Good. Uses informal 'tu' form. 'Su nombre' could be his/her/your(formal).

phrases.english: with everyone else
phrases.other: con todos los demás
phrases.notes: Perfect idiomatic expression.

phrases.english: she wanted to ask you how long you have been
phrases.other: ella quería preguntarte cuánto tiempo llevas
phrases.notes: INCOMPLETE - Missing verb/activity. 'How long you have been' WHAT? Spanish 'llevas' implies duration but sentence trails off.

phrases.english: or if I need to speak Spanish very well this morning
phrases.other: o si necesito hablar español muy bien esta mañana
phrases.notes: Grammatically correct but semantically odd - why would one 'need' to speak very well specifically 'this morning'?

phrases.english: why do you want to start talking
phrases.other: por qué quieres empezar a hablar
phrases.notes: Natural both. 'Empezar a + infinitive' correct.

phrases.english: I wanted to ask you how you feel
phrases.other: quería preguntarte cómo te sientes
phrases.notes: Perfect. Imperfect 'quería' for polite softening, reflexive 'sentirse' correct.

phrases.english: I wanted to ask you yesterday
phrases.other: quería preguntarte ayer
phrases.notes: Natural both languages.

phrases.english: but I don't want to stop talking this evening
phrases.other: pero no quiero dejar de hablar esta noche
phrases.notes: Perfect. 'Dejar de + infinitive' correctly means 'to stop doing'.

phrases.english: we don't want to now
phrases.other: no queremos ahora
phrases.notes: English incomplete - 'want to' what? Spanish similarly elliptical. Only works with strong context.

phrases.english: as quickly as possible
phrases.other: lo más rápido posible
phrases.notes: Perfect idiomatic expression.

phrases.english: taking time to answer
phrases.other: tomar tiempo para responder
phrases.notes: English uses gerund, Spanish uses infinitive. 'Tomándose tiempo' or 'tomarse el tiempo' would be more natural Spanish.

phrases.english: he wants to find out
phrases.other: él quiere saber
phrases.notes: Good translation. 'Saber' captures 'find out' well in this context.

phrases.english: and I want you to speak Spanish with me tomorrow
phrases.other: y quiero que hables español conmigo mañana
phrases.notes: Perfect. Subjunctive 'hables' correctly used after 'quiero que'.

phrases.english: I want to know why she wants to learn more later on
phrases.other: quiero saber por qué ella quiere aprender más más tarde
phrases.notes: 'más más tarde' sounds awkward - 'más' (more) followed by 'más tarde' (later). Consider 'aprender más tarde' or restructure.

phrases.english: after you finish I'd like to try
phrases.other: después de que termines me gustaría intentar
phrases.notes: Correct subjunctive 'termines' after 'después de que'. Natural both languages.

phrases.english: and we want to meet at six o'clock tomorrow
phrases.other: y queremos reunirnos a las seis mañana
phrases.notes: Natural. Reflexive 'reunirnos' correct for 'to meet (each other)'.

phrases.english: before I have to go
phrases.other: antes de que tenga que irme
phrases.notes: Perfect. Subjunctive 'tenga' correct after 'antes de que'. Reflexive 'irme' natural.

phrases.english: I don't care if I need to improve today and I feel okay
phrases.other: no me importa si necesito mejorar hoy y me siento bien
phrases.notes: Long but correct. Compound structure works in both languages.

phrases.english: I was starting to feel better but I am tired at the moment
phrases.other: estaba empezando a sentirme mejor pero estoy cansado en este momento
phrases.notes: Good contrast of imperfect 'estaba' with present 'estoy'. Natural construction.

phrases.english: I want to learn something
phrases.other: quiero aprender algo
phrases.notes: Perfect. Simple and natural.

phrases.english: and I would like to be able to speak Spanish very well
phrases.other: y me gustaría poder hablar español muy bien
phrases.notes: Natural. 'Poder' + infinitive structure correct.

phrases.english: it's useful now
phrases.other: es útil ahora
phrases.notes: Perfect. Simple and clean.

phrases.english: why do you want to be able to remember her name quickly
phrases.other: por qué quieres poder recordar su nombre rápidamente
phrases.notes: Correct but lengthy. Natural enough in both languages.

phrases.english: I like feeling as if I'm nearly ready
phrases.other: me gusta sentirme como si estuviera casi listo
phrases.notes: Good. Imperfect subjunctive 'estuviera' correct after 'como si'. Note: 'listo' masculine.

phrases.english: I want to try to remember the whole sentence now
phrases.other: quiero intentar recordar toda la frase ahora
phrases.notes: Perfect. Verb chain natural, 'toda la frase' correct.

phrases.english: I'm going to try to say something in Spanish
phrases.other: voy a intentar decir algo en español
phrases.notes: Perfect. 'Ir a + infinitive' for near future, natural verb chain.

phrases.english: we want to meet with everyone else tomorrow
phrases.other: queremos reunirnos con todos los demás mañana
phrases.notes: Perfect. 'Reunirnos con' natural construction.

phrases.english: I think that it's like this
phrases.other: creo que es así
phrases.notes: Perfect. Idiomatic use of 'así'.

phrases.english: I'm not trying because I feel okay
phrases.other: no estoy intentando porque me siento bien
phrases.notes: English slightly odd without context (not trying to do what?). Spanish grammatically correct.

phrases.english: I feel better today than last night
phrases.other: me siento mejor hoy que anoche
phrases.notes: Perfect. Natural comparison structure.

phrases.english: or if I need to improve now
phrases.other: o si necesito mejorar ahora
phrases.notes: Natural fragment, clean construction.

phrases.english: I'm trying to speak Spanish with someone else now
phrases.other: estoy intentando hablar español con alguien más ahora
phrases.notes: Natural. 'Alguien más' correct for 'someone else'.

phrases.english: she doesn't want to speak
phrases.other: ella no quiere hablar
phrases.notes: Perfect. Simple and natural.

phrases.english: I'm going to feel as if I'm nearly ready soon
phrases.other: voy a sentirme como si estuviera casi listo pronto
phrases.notes: Correct but complex. Imperfect subjunctive 'estuviera' correct. Slightly dense construction.
